# Individual Plots

```{r auditory_plot}
auditory_long <- auditory |>
  filter(Status=="Longitudinal") |>
   mutate(
    `Age (wks)` = as.numeric(`Age (wks)`),
    `Proportion Correct` = as.numeric(`Proportion Correct`),
     `experience` = as.numeric(`# Prior Test Sessions`)
  )

auditory_plot <- auditory_long|>
  ggplot(aes(x=`Age (wks)`, y = `Proportion Correct`))+
  geom_jitter(alpha=0.2, width = 0.05, height = 0.05)+
  geom_smooth(method="loess", color = "black") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "",
    limits = c(8, 20), 
    breaks = seq(8, 20, by = 2)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1), 
    breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25),
    labels = as.character
  ) +
  labs(title = "Auditory Discrimination")

print(auditory_plot)
```

# Per-Task Models (Longitudinal)

```{r models_long}
task_models <- function(df) {
  
m_age <- glmer(cbind(`Trials Correct`, `Total Trials` - `Trials Correct`) ~ `Age (wks)` + (1 | `Dog ID`),
                 family = binomial, data = df)
m_exp <- glmer(cbind(`Trials Correct`, `Total Trials` - `Trials Correct`) ~ `Age (wks)` + experience + (1 | `Dog ID`),
                 family = binomial, data = df) 

tibble(AIC_age = AIC(m_age), AIC_age_exp = AIC(m_exp))
  }

aic_tibble <- bind_rows(
  "Marker gesture"               = task_models(marker_long),
  "Working memory (Delay)"       = task_models(workingmem_long),
  "Working memory (Distraction)" = task_models(distraction_long),
  "Auditory discrimination"      = task_models(auditory_long),
  "Odor discrimination"         = task_models(odor_long),
  "Cylinder: inhibitory control" = task_models(detour_long),
  "Cylinder: reversal learning"  = task_models(reversal_long),
  "Causal reasoning"             = task_models(causal_long),
  "Momentary pointing"           = task_models(momentary_long),
  .id="Task") |> 
  mutate(Best = if_else(AIC_age_exp < AIC_age, "age + experience", "age"))

aic_tibble

```

```{r proplook_models_long}

m_age <- glmer(cbind(`# Trials Looked`, `Total Trials` - `# Trials Looked`) ~ `Age (wks)` + (1 | `Dog ID`),
               family = binomial, data = unsolvable_long)
m_exp <- glmer(cbind(`# Trials Looked`, `Total Trials` - `# Trials Looked`) ~ `Age (wks)` + experience + (1 | `Dog ID`),
               family = binomial, data = unsolvable_long)

aic_tibble2 <- tibble(AIC_age = AIC(m_age), AIC_age_exp = AIC(m_exp))|>
  mutate(Best = if_else(AIC_age_exp < AIC_age, "age + experience", "age"))

aic_tibble2
```

```{r looktime_models_long}

m_age <- lmer(`Mean Look Time` ~ `Age (wks)` + (1 | `Dog ID`),
              data = unsolvable_long, REML = FALSE)
m_exp <- lmer(`Mean Look Time` ~ `Age (wks)` + experience + (1 | `Dog ID`),
              data = unsolvable_long, REML = FALSE)


aic_tibble3 <- tibble(AIC_age = AIC(m_age), AIC_age_exp = AIC(m_exp))|>
  mutate(Best = if_else(AIC_age_exp < AIC_age, "age + experience", "age"))

aic_tibble3
```

`correct ~ age + (1 | puppy_ID)` is better for:

- Marker Gesture (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble$AIC_age[aic_tibble$Task == "Marker gesture"], 1)`)

- Working Memory with Distraction (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble$AIC_age[aic_tibble$Task == "Working memory (Distraction)"], 1)`)

- Odor Discrimination (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble$AIC_age[aic_tibble$Task == "Odor discrimination"], 1)`)

- Unsolvable Proportion Looked (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble2$AIC_age, 1)`)

- Unsolvable Average Looking Time (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble3$AIC_age, 1)`).

`correct ~ age + experience + (1 | puppy_ID)` is better for:

- Working Memory with Delay (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble$AIC_age_exp[aic_tibble$Task == "Working memory (Delay)"], 1)`)

- Auditory Discrimination (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble$AIC_age_exp[aic_tibble$Task == "Auditory discrimination"], 1)`)

- Cylinder Inhibitory Control (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble$AIC_age_exp[aic_tibble$Task == "Cylinder: inhibitory control"], 1)`)

- Cylinder Reversal Learning (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble$AIC_age_exp[aic_tibble$Task == "Cylinder: reversal learning"], 1)`)

- Causal Reasoning (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble$AIC_age_exp[aic_tibble$Task == "Causal reasoning"], 1)`).

- Momentary Pointing (AIC = `r round(aic_tibble$AIC_age_exp[aic_tibble$Task == "Momentary pointing"], 1)`).

# Model Build Up (for 9 two-choice tasks)

```{r confirmatory_data}

all_tasks <- bind_rows(
  "Marker gesture"               = marker_long,
  "Working memory (Delay)"       = workingmem_long,
  "Working memory (Distraction)" = distraction_long,
  "Auditory discrimination"      = auditory_long,
  "Odor discrimination"          = odor_long,
  "Cylinder: inhibitory control" = detour_long,
  "Cylinder: reversal learning"  = reversal_long,
  "Causal reasoning"             = causal_long,
  "Momentary pointing"           = momentary_long,
  .id = "task") |>
  transmute(task,
            id      = factor(`Dog ID`),
            age     = `Age (wks)` - 8,
            correct = `Trials Correct`,
            total   = `Total Trials`)

ctrl <- glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

r_age_exp <- bind_rows(marker_long, workingmem_long, distraction_long, auditory_long,
                       odor_long, detour_long, reversal_long, causal_long,
                       momentary_long, unsolvable_long) |>
  summarise(r = cor(`Age (wks)`, `# Prior Test Sessions`)) |>
  pull(r)

```

```{r model_buildup}
# random intercepts only
m1 <- glmer(cbind(correct, total - correct) ~ age * task + (1 | id) + (1 | id:task),
            family = binomial, data = all_tasks, control = ctrl)

# by-puppy random slope for age
m2 <- glmer(cbind(correct, total - correct) ~ age * task + (1 + age | id) + (1 | id:task),
            family = binomial, data = all_tasks, control = ctrl)

isSingular(m2)   # TRUE = random effects too complex for the data
anova(m1, m2)    # does the random slope improve fit?

# same slope as m2, no intercept-slope correlation
m3 <- glmer(cbind(correct, total - correct) ~ age * task + (1 + age || id) + (1 | id:task),
            family = binomial, data = all_tasks, control = ctrl)

isSingular(m3)    # FALSE = fitted cleanly
anova(m1, m3)     # no sig improvement, m1 has slightly better AIC

```

```{r interaction_test}
# m3 most complex model that converged without warnings
m_final <- m3

# KEY RESULT: age x task interaction
m_final_noint <- update(m_final, . ~ . - age:task)
anova(m_final_noint, m_final)

# m1 has marginally lower AIC so using as robustness check
m_final2 <- m1

# age x task interaction
m_final2_noint <- update(m_final2, . ~ . - age:task)
anova(m_final2_noint, m_final2)

```

```{r 113pups_exp}

all_tasks_all <- bind_rows(
  "Marker gesture"               = marker,
  "Working memory (Delay)"       = workingmem,
  "Working memory (Distraction)" = distraction,
  "Auditory discrimination"      = auditory,
  "Odor discrimination"          = odor,
  "Cylinder: inhibitory control" = detour,
  "Cylinder: reversal learning"  = reversal,
  "Causal reasoning"             = causal,
  "Momentary pointing"           = momentary,
  .id = "task") |>
  transmute(task,
            id         = factor(`Dog ID`),
            age        = `Age (wks)` - 8,
            experience = `# Prior Test Sessions`,
            correct    = `Trials Correct`,
            total      = `Total Trials`)

cor(all_tasks_all$age, all_tasks_all$experience)   #0.76

# Each task gets its own age slope AND its own experience slope
m_ae <- glmer(cbind(correct, total - correct) ~ age * task + experience * task +
                (1 | id) + (1 | id:task),
              family = binomial, data = all_tasks_all, control = ctrl)

# Does age x task matter AFTER accounting for task-specific experience effects?
m_ae_noint <- update(m_ae, . ~ . - age:task)
lrt_ae <- anova(m_ae_noint, m_ae)
lrt_ae
```

The age × task interaction was significant in the random-slope model (m3), χ²(`r lrt_m3$Df[2]`) = `r round(lrt_m3$Chisq[2], 2)`, p `r format.pval(lrt_m3$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2], digits = 2, eps = .001)`, and in the random-intercepts model (m1), χ²(`r lrt_m1$Df[2]`) = `r round(lrt_m1$Chisq[2], 2)`, p `r format.pval(lrt_m1$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2], digits = 2, eps = .001)`. This indicates that the 9 tasks do not share one developmental rate, consistent with the multiple intelligences hypothesis. Because age and experience are highly correlated in the longitudinal puppies (r = `r round(r_age_exp, 2)`), this model cannot disentangle the model whether these task differences reflect maturation, accumulated testing experience, or both.

After adding the 22 control puppies and task-specific experience effects, the age × task interaction was still significant, χ²(`r lrt_ae$Df[2]`) = `r round(lrt_ae$Chisq[2], 2)`, p `r format.pval(lrt_ae$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2], digits = 2, eps = .001)`. While part of the longitudinal age × task interaction effect may be shared with experience , the results from the 113-subject sample further support the multiple intelligences hypothesis, although age and experience remain partly correlated (r = `r round(cor(all_tasks_all$age, all_tasks_all$experience), 2)`).
